claims: The Jones Act is the Merchant Marine Act of 1920.
The Jones Act is a federal law.
The Jones Act requires that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on ships that are U.S.-built, U.S.-owned, and crewed by U.S. citizens.
Foreign-flagged vessels are prohibited from transporting cargo or passengers directly between two U.S. ports.
The Jones Act grants injured seamen the right to seek damages from employers through jury trials.
The Jones Act can be temporarily waived for reasons of national defense by the Department of Homeland Security or the Department of Defense.
